analyst_note: The project IPEDS series reports 162 U.S. nonresident students in Fall 2023 and 81 in Fall 2024, a decline of 81, with undergraduate/graduate components of 76/86 and 43/38. New Mexico Highlands University's official end-of-term Student Enrollment by Ethnicity & Gender reports use the same Non Resident Alien label and imply 157 students in Fall 2023 (60 male and 97 female) and 86 in Fall 2024 (26 male and 60 female), a decline of 71. The institutional undergraduate/graduate components are 76/81 in 2023 and 44/42 in 2024, including an exact match to the 2023 IPEDS undergraduate component and endpoint all-student differences of only five students in each year. The institutional all-student totals are 2,842 and 2,743 versus IPEDS 2,814 and 2,704, consistent with the reports' end-of-term timing rather than an assumed fall-census identity. Do not substitute the institutional counts for IPEDS. The close same-label two-year series independently corroborates the scale and direction of the decline, supporting bounded discussion while IPEDS remains the numerical authority.

The project IPEDS series reports 124 U.S. nonresident students in Fall 2023 and 202 in Fall 2024, an increase of 78 (+62.9%), with all 202 students reported at the undergraduate level. Vincennes University's official August 23, 2024 enrollment announcement, issued during the first week of the 2024-25 academic year, states that preliminary first-day figures showed a rise in international students on the Vincennes Campus and through online programs. Approved August 21, 2024 Board of Trustees minutes likewise state that international student numbers on the Vincennes Campus and online were growing while discussing Fall 2024 enrollment. Those contemporaneous institutional statements independently corroborate the direction of the Fall 2023-to-Fall 2024 increase. They do not provide comparable endpoint counts, a final census-date population, or evidence that the university-defined international population is definition-identical to IPEDS U.S. nonresident status. Preserve IPEDS as the numerical authority and clear only bounded direction-level discussion of the +78 movement; do not infer an institutional headcount from the qualitative growth statement.
